newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks end strong as banks, China-plays surge.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks end strong as banks, China-plays surge.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks finished on a strong note on Friday as hopes that the market had hit a short-term bottom spurred buying in the banking sector, while China-plays also benefited from keen interest.
The Hang Seng Index closed on a gain of 157.90 points, or 1.28 percent, at 12,516.60, bringing the week's gains to 312.01 points, or 2.56 percent.
Turnover was HK$9.33 billion compared with HK$8.18 billion.
"It seems like turnover is picking up so buying interest is also recovering," said Ben Kwong, director of research at Dharmala Securities.
He said Hong Kong shares had been hovering at lower levels over recent sessions without meeting strong selling pressure and Wall Street share prices seemed to have stabilised after a recent decline.
"Investors have already discounted some of the concern about an interest rate hike so there is continued bargain-hunting at lower levels," said Kwong.
Analysts said banking shares had been oversold and were the main beneficiaries of bargain-hunting. HSBC Holdings rose HK$3.00 to HK$184.00 and Hang Seng Bank gained HK$1.75 to HK$81.50.

"Over the last couple of weeks, people were concerned about rising interest rates in the U.S. but now inflation in China is coming down and investors are expecting China to lower interest rates," said Yamaichi International head of research Alex Tang.
China's retail price inflation rose 1.7 percent in March following retail price inflation of 2.9 percent in February.

An official at China's State Planning Commission Economic Research Institute said on Friday that China's benchmark retail price inflation could slow more quickly than expected in 1997, to three to four percent for the year.

The H-share index surged 29.88 points to 1,034.90. Among the red chips, Shanghai Industrial jumped HK$1.90 to HK$37.70, China Resources advanced HK$0.60 to HK$17.95 and CITIC Pacific gained HK$0.50 to HK$38.20.
China Light rose HK$0.80 to HK$35.30 following news that it had signed a Shenzhen power plant joint venture agreement with Exxon Corp.
In the property sector, Sun Hung Kai Properties gained HK$1.25 to HK$77.75 and Cheung Kong rose HK$0.75 to HK$65.50.
